name: core-date-timezone-runtime-depth
salesforceExclusionReason: This fixture proves deterministic local Date, Time, and TimeZone runtime behavior and makes no Salesforce parity claim.

source.content: Date leap = Date.newInstance(2024, 2, 29); Date monthEnd = Date.newInstance(2024, 1, 31); System.assertEquals(Date.newInstance(2024, 2, 29), monthEnd.addMonths(1)); System.assertEquals(Date.newInstance(2025, 1, 31), monthEnd.addYears(1)); System.assert(leap.equals(leap)); System.assert(leap.hashCode() != null); System.assert(leap.toString().contains('2024-02-29')); Date today = Date.today(); System.assert(today <= Date.today()); Time clock = Time.newInstance(12, 34, 56, 789); System.assert(clock.equals(clock)); System.assert(clock.hashCode() != null); System.assertEquals('12:34:56.789Z', clock.toString()); TimeZone utc = TimeZone.getTimeZone('UTC'); TimeZone cloned = (TimeZone) utc.clone(); System.assertEquals('UTC', utc.getID()); System.assertEquals(0, utc.getOffset(Datetime.newInstanceGmt(2024, 7, 1, 12, 0, 0))); System.assert(utc.toString() != null); System.assert(cloned != null);
